blocks.content: Generation data now reaches Agent Observability. The SDK also emits OpenTelemetry spans and four `gen_ai.client.*` metrics, but it does not create OpenTelemetry providers. Without a `TracerProvider` and `MeterProvider` in your application they are dropped.

Open the Grafana Cloud portal at `https://grafana.com/orgs/{org}/stacks/{stack-id}` and copy the two values from the **OpenTelemetry** card.

- **OTLP endpoint URL**, including `/otlp` but excluding signal paths such as `/v1/traces`. This is the value for `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT`.
- **Instance ID** on the OpenTelemetry card. This is the basic-auth username for OTLP and can differ from the Agent Observability **Instance ID** from Milestone 2.

> **Note:** Don't click **Generate now**. The access policy token from Milestone 3 already covers `metrics:write`, `logs:write`, and `traces:write`.
Save them somewhere you can find them later, such as a notes file.

Copy the following command into the shell from Milestone 4. Do not run it yet.

```bash
printf '%s' '{OTLP_INSTANCE_ID}:{ACCESS_POLICY_TOKEN}' | base64 | tr -d '\n'
```

The `tr -d '\n'` is not optional. `base64` adds a trailing newline that invalidates the header.

Replace the placeholders in that command.

Replace `{OTLP_INSTANCE_ID}` with the OpenTelemetry **Instance ID**. Replace `{ACCESS_POLICY_TOKEN}` with the access policy token from Milestone 3.
Run the command.

blocks.authorNote: TODO (open question 12, also on journey slide 32): Is `%20` in `Authorization=Basic%20<BASE64_CREDENTIALS>` required for every language's OTLP exporter, or only for Python? The Set up Agent Observability page shows `Basic%20` and says it is for the Python exporter; the SDK configuration page shows a literal space for every language. If Python only, this block should show the generic form and say Python needs `%20`; if it differs by language, this block needs a per-language line. Who answers: the Agent Observability docs owner, with the SDK owners. Remove this note once answered.
blocks.content:
Copy the following commands into that same shell. Do not run them yet.

`export` sets each variable in that shell so the exporters can read it.

```bash
export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT="{OTLP_ENDPOINT}"
export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS="Authorization=Basic%20{BASE64_CREDENTIALS}"
```

Copy the output of the `printf` command.

It is the one line still on screen above these commands, with no newline at the end.
Paste that output into `{BASE64_CREDENTIALS}` in the commands you just copied.

Replace `{OTLP_ENDPOINT}` with the OTLP endpoint URL.

Keep `%20` for the space after `Basic`.
Run the commands.

Add a `TracerProvider` and a `MeterProvider` to your sample before you create the client, and shut them down after the client's shutdown call.

Copy the snippet for your language from [OpenTelemetry setup](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana-cloud/observe-and-act/agent-observability/instrumentation/sdk/#opentelemetry-setup). The Python version is also shown under [Configure providers in your application](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana-cloud/observe-and-act/agent-observability/get-started/grafana-cloud/#configure-providers-in-your-application). The snippets set `service.name` to `my-agent`.
Run the sample again from the same shell.
The sample has been rerun with the providers in place.
Check the Traces data source for your agent's spans.
Go to **Drilldown** > **Traces**.

Select a time range that covers the rerun.

For example, **Last 15 minutes**.
Open **Traces**.
blocks.hint: Open **Breakdown** and group by `resource.service.name` to see `my-agent` as its own value.

blocks.content:
Look for spans from `my-agent`.

That is the `service.name` set in the provider snippet.
Spans from the rerun appear under the `my-agent` service in your Grafana Cloud Traces data source.
Check the Metrics data source for the SDK's metrics.
Go to **Drilldown** > **Metrics**.

In the search box, type `gen_ai`.

This filters the metric list to the SDK's metrics.

Confirm the list shows the SDK's metrics.

The names are `gen_ai_client_operation_duration`, `gen_ai_client_token_usage`, `gen_ai_client_time_to_first_token`, and `gen_ai_client_tool_calls_per_operation`. Prometheus stores the OpenTelemetry dot names with underscores.
The SDK's metrics are in your Grafana Cloud Metrics data source.

No spans or metrics? Check these in order:

1. The providers are configured before the client is created, and shut down after `client.shutdown()`.
2. `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` was built with the OTLP **Instance ID** from the OpenTelemetry card, not the Agent Observability **Instance ID**, and with `tr -d '\n'`.
3. `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` ends in `/otlp` with no `/v1/traces` or `/v1/metrics` suffix.
4. The access policy from Milestone 3 has `metrics:write` and `traces:write` selected.
